questions: With a player that never names a move, what becomes of each plain line that wants one — rolled, offered on a button, read as another move, or narrated with nothing offered — and how many beats come to their last resort?
Does the player in fact stay in the fiction: how many lines name a move outside a last resort, and does play still reach every beat within the run's caps?
Are the memory questions asked with @scene answered plainly and rightly, with no invented speaker — including facts planted in an earlier session (sets B and C)?
The four questions left as lines of play: are they still answered through an invented all-knowing voice, and are they offered a move?
Is the fight begun this time (its card after the roll, "Begin the fight"), and do the miss's price, the burn, the GM's reload mid-fight and Take Decisive Action hold? (Run 2 exercised none of them.)
Do the fixes made after run 2 hold in play from plain lines: a recovery line offered its move, a full relationship track read as Forge a Bond, a corrected or changed name not told as a story?
Is a step toward the vow said in the fiction read as a milestone, or narrated with nothing offered, as the readers' test found twelve times in twelve?
Does the narrator still return to one detail beat after beat and close each beat on someone waiting — counted — and does any narration write its outcome's label ("Strong hit…") into the prose?
Does each recap sentence match the transcript?
Beats done, checks violated, cost and a line's wait against runs 1 and 2.

Haiku 5.5 costs five times these rates on a prompt over 100,000 tokens; the module's prompts are a few thousand.
